newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- CO-OP TO PROSECUTE FAILED BIDDER

With the withdrawal out of one of his main financial backers, Nomura International, the Co-Operative Wholesale Society has begun a private prosecution of Andrew Regan for aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring theft and or handling stolen property. NI pulled out after they failed to receive assurance of the integrity of the participants in the deal. The CWS will also try to permanently prevent the use of confidential CWS information obtained by Regan and his associate David Lyons. The criminal proceedings will begin on May 28th in London.
-- EUROTUNNEL SEEKS 999-YEAR LEASE TO WIN OVER INVESTORS

Eurotunnel has insisted that French and British governments extend its 65-year lease to operate Channel tunnels to a 999-year lease. The Eurotunnel chairman claims a longer lease would ensure longer revenue streams and in turn secure investors for its proposed 8.4-billion financial restructuring. London and Continental Railways have already received 999-year concessions to build a high-speed link between the tunnel and London.
-- HYUNDAI LOOKS AT BUILDING LARGE CAR FACTORY IN UK

South Korean car manufacturer Hyundai is said to consider the UK a favourable candidate site for its European plant that is expected to build 100,000 cars a year. The plant would be opened before the end of the decade and bring along the creation at least 2,000 jobs with many more in UK and European components industries. The leading contenders are Bristol's Portbury Docks, Sunderland in Tyne and Ware, and Scotland.
-- EMU POLICY LEAVES UK BANKING IN DISARRAY

UK banks are said to be in a state of disarray following the government's wait-and-see policy on the single currency issue. The Bank of England has declared some UK banks have now become "complacent" in their preparations for EMU. The banks state that preparation for single currency is difficult as no one is quite sure if or when Britain will join EMU.
-- BRUSSELS TO GET WIDER POWERS ON VETTING MERGERS

Britain has dropped all of its objections to allotting the EU the power to vet cross-border mergers. The announcement awards the EU new life in its desire to reform EU anti-monopoly rules, such as restricting mergers that could damage competition in the single market. Britain had originally objected because it did not want the EU to interfere with mergers that would have fallen under the jurisdiction of its own Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
-- COMPETITIVE WATER SUPPLIERS FACE HOSTILITY

The Environment Agency has confirmed it will approve the proposal of entrepreneur Ray Edmed to operate a currently unused borehole to sell water to Cott Europe, manufacturer of Virgin Cola. Yorkshire water, who currently serves Cott, has taken opposition the announcement and declined to lend its pipes to Edmed to transport the water. New proposals from Ofwat called "inset arrangements" allow competition for customers of a rival, but Edmed's plans do not come under the arrangements.
-- BA TO LAND TERMINAL 5 SITE

According to BAA, the new fifth terminal at Heathrow airport will be occupied by British Airways and its partners conditional on planning permission, but its opening has been delayed two years until 2004. BA claim its move to the new terminal would be an asset as they would no longer be required to split services between terminals one and four. American Airlines is rumoured to be linking up with British Airways and Quantas of Australia to occupy Terminal Five.
-- REPORT DUE ON N IRELAND POWER

Rumours that the Monopolies and Mergers Commission will reject Ofreg's proposal for a 31 percent cut in the price of electricity at Northern Ireland Electricity will be confirmed on Friday, as it is expected the MMC will release its report. NIE has proposed a counter offer for a 22 percent cut, but it is expected the MME would compromise at a 25 percent reduction. NIE chairman David Jeffries has warned the decision will have a significant impact on the company's future income.
-- STRONG POUND LIFTS ICI PROFITS IN FIRST QUARTER

Leading European company Imperial Chemical Industries has announced third quarter pre-tax profits down one third from a year ago due to falling prices and the strength of sterling. ICI is in the bidding for the chemicals division of Unilever, which would not only stretch the company financially but also go against its current move away from industrial chemicals and towards specialty chemicals.
-- ENI PICKS LONDON AS BASE FOR OVERSEAS EXPANSION

Italian oil and gas group Eni plans to move a section of its international operations from Milan to London in a corporate restructuring move to make the company a true multinational. Eni chose London because of its growing importance as a centre of the international oil and gas industry. The move is currently in the planning stage and it has not yet been determined how many people will be involved.
